raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`UnifiedSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator.reclaim_plan` computes the joint FULL/SWA eviction quotas with a fixed priority: it first finds the least SWA reclaim that fits with every evictable FULL token available, then trims FULL. That spends FULL prefix before it touches the sliding window.

Two configurations want the opposite priority:

- a HiCache storage backend is attached: the FULL prefix is the part of the tree that storage can serve again, so it is the part worth keeping resident;
- the engine is the decode side of a PD pair: the device prefix arrives by transfer rather than by local prefill.

## Modifications

- `reclaim_plan(..., prefer_swa=False)`: with `prefer_swa` the same two-pass search runs with the roles swapped, i.e. least FULL reclaim first, then least SWA reclaim.
- `evict_to_free_tokens` selects `prefer_swa` when `enable_hierarchical_cache` is set and `hicache_storage_backend` is not `None`, or when `disaggregation_mode == "decode"`. The leaves are read per call because the storage attach/detach endpoints and PD role switching change them at runtime.
- Only the quotas handed to the tree change. Victim selection, eviction cascades, locks, compaction gates and capacity checks are untouched; direct component eviction and `evict_for_alloc` keep their original order.

## Tests

`test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_multi_ended_allocator.py`:

- `test_reclaim_plan_matches_exhaustive_page_targets` now also asserts the `prefer_swa=True` plan equals the lexicographic (FULL, SWA) minimum of the feasible set, next to the existing (SWA, FULL) check.
- `test_evict_to_free_tokens_prefers_swa_reclaim_on_storage_or_decode` pins the planner argument for four configurations: default and hierarchical-cache-only keep FULL-first; storage backend and decode role switch to SWA-first.

Both are red on main (`reclaim_plan` rejects the keyword; the argument is absent) and green here. The ten CPU unit files that build the unified SWA allocator (`test_multi_ended_allocator`, `test_prefill_memory_budget`, `test_unified_radix_allocation_eviction`, `test_swa_locked_full_recover_unified`, `test_unified_byte_accounting`, `test_unified_tri_pool`, `test_unified_capacity_memo`, `test_unified_free_no_host_sync`, `test_unified_swa_shared_virtual_ids`, `disaggregation/test_unified_memory_move_gate`) pass with the change.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation).
- [ ] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.html) and [Accuracy Results](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#accuracy-results).
- [ ] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging.
- [ ] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss your PR.

@@ -908,12 +909,14 @@ def reclaim_plan(
         full_evictable_tokens: int = 0,
         swa_evictable_tokens: int = 0,
         empty_pool: bool = False,
+        prefer_swa: bool = False,
     ) -> Optional[Tuple[int, int]]:
         """Return cumulative FULL/SWA eviction targets, or None if impossible.
 
         The tree evicts FULL before SWA. Minimize required SWA reclaim with all
         evictable FULL available, then trim excess FULL reclaim. FULL eviction's
         actual SWA cascade is counted by the tree's shared eviction tracker.
+        With ``prefer_swa``, minimize FULL reclaim first and trim SWA instead.
         """
         if full_tokens < 0 or swa_tokens < 0:
             return None
@@ -962,12 +965,20 @@ def first_fit(high: int, predicate: Callable[[int], bool]) -> int:
                     low = mid + 1
             return low
 
-        swa_reclaim_pages = first_fit(
-            max_swa_pages, lambda value: fits(max_full_pages, value)
-        )
-        full_reclaim_pages = first_fit(
-            max_full_pages, lambda value: fits(value, swa_reclaim_pages)
-        )
+        if prefer_swa:
+            full_reclaim_pages = first_fit(
+                max_full_pages, lambda value: fits(value, max_swa_pages)
+            )

+        else:

         return (

@@ -686,6 +692,55 @@ def test_reclaim_plan_matches_exhaustive_page_targets(self):
                                 ),
                                 feasible[0] if feasible else None,
                             )
+                            # ``prefer_swa`` flips the lexicographic order:
+                            # least FULL reclaim first, then least SWA.
+                            self.assertEqual(
+                                allocator.reclaim_plan(
+                                    full_pages * page_size,
+                                    swa_pages * page_size,
+                                    full_evictable_tokens=full_evictable,
+                                    swa_evictable_tokens=swa_evictable,
+                                    prefer_swa=True,
+                                ),
+                                min(feasible) if feasible else None,
+                            )
+
+    def test_evict_to_free_tokens_prefers_swa_reclaim_on_storage_or_decode(self):
+        """The default quota order spends FULL prefix to keep the sliding
+        window. With a HiCache storage backend attached, or while serving as
+        the decode side of a PD pair, the FULL prefix is the one worth keeping,
+        so the allocator asks the planner for SWA-first quotas. Hierarchical
+        cache alone (no storage backend) keeps the default. Pins the planner
+        argument per configuration, so a predicate that degrades to one branch
+        is caught."""
+        _, allocator, _ = self._build(page_size=4)
+        tree_cache = MagicMock()
+        tree_cache.supports_prefix_sharing.return_value = True
+        tree_cache.full_evictable_size.return_value = 8
+        tree_cache.swa_evictable_size.return_value = 8
+        allocator.reclaim_plan = MagicMock(return_value=(0, 0))
+        cases = (
+            ({}, None, False),
+            ({"enable_hierarchical_cache": True}, None, False),
+            (
+                {"enable_hierarchical_cache": True, "hicache_storage_backend": "file"},
+                None,
+                True,
+            ),
+            ({}, "decode", True),
+        )
+        for memory, role, prefer_swa in cases:
+            with self.subTest(memory=memory, role=role):
+                with contextlib.ExitStack() as stack:
+                    stack.enter_context(get_memory().override(**memory))
+                    if role is not None:
+                        stack.enter_context(
+                            get_disagg().override(disaggregation_mode=role)
+                        )
+                    allocator.evict_to_free_tokens(tree_cache, 4)
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    allocator.reclaim_plan.call_args.kwargs["prefer_swa"], prefer_swa
+                )
 
     def test_restore_swa_without_allocating_more_full(self):
         _, allocator, _ = self._build(page_size=4)
